The Central Sierra Miwok are a Miwok people of the western foothills of the Sierra Nevada in California, along the Stanislaus and Tuolumne rivers. They lived in villages of bark houses, gathered acorns, which they ground and leached into meal, and hunted deer.

Their land was the heart of the Mother Lode, where the Gold Rush began in 1848. Miners overran it within a few years, bringing disease, massacres and the loss of the food that the land had given. Survivors worked in mines and ranches. Today the Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk and the Chicken Ranch Rancheria are among their tribes. Neighbours: Northern Sierra Miwok and Yokuts.
